setup: For \(A = \begin{pmatrix} [[a]] & [[b]] \\ [[c]] & [[d]] \end{pmatrix}\), \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\det A}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}\): swap the diagonal entries, negate the others, divide by the determinant.

steps.say: Swapping the diagonal puts \(d = [[d]]\) in the first row, first column; dividing by the determinant [[determinant]] leaves [[entry]].

answer: So the first-row, first-column entry of \(A^{-1}\) is [[entry]].
